Buttery Martinstag Buns

Served at: Martinstag Lantern Evening

Makes 12 buns (Serves 8-10)Prep 2 hours (includes rising time)Cook 20-25 min

Martinstag, celebrated on November 11th, commemorates Saint Martin of Tours with lantern parades and community gatherings. These tender, buttery buns are a comforting treat, perfect for warming up little hands after a lantern walk, offering a sweet and simple indulgence to share with family and friends.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar, plus 1 teaspoon
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons (7 g) active dry yeast (1 standard packet)
  • 3 1/2 cups (420 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly
  • 1 large egg, at room temperature
  • 1 large egg yolk
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) water or milk

Method

  1. Gently warm the milk in a small saucepan or microwave until it is lukewarm (105-115°F / 40-46°C). Stir in 1 teaspoon of granulated sugar, then sprinkle the active dry yeast over the milk. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, the remaining 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar, and salt.
  3. Pour the yeast mixture, melted butter, and the whole egg into the dry ingredients. Mix with a wooden spoon or a stand mixer with a dough hook until a shaggy dough forms.
  4. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes, or use a stand mixer with a dough hook on medium-low speed for 6-8 minutes, until the dough is smooth and elastic.
  5. Lightly grease a clean bowl with oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
  6. Once doubled, gently punch down the dough to release the air. Turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and divide it into 12 equal pieces. Shape each piece into a smooth round bun.
  7. Place the shaped buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving some space between them. Cover loosely with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let them rise again for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
  8. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). In a small bowl, whisk together the egg yolk and 1 tablespoon of water or milk to create an egg wash.
  9. Gently brush the tops of the risen buns with the egg wash.
  10. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the buns are golden brown on top and sound hollow when tapped on the bottom. Transfer to a wire rack to cool slightly before serving.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, add 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract or the zest of half a lemon to the dough along with the wet ingredients.
  • Traditionally, some Martinstag pastries are shaped like geese or little men (Weckmänner). You can try shaping a few buns this way before the second rise.
  • Serve these buttery buns warm, perhaps with a little extra butter, jam, or honey, perfect for a cozy evening.
